categories.main_business_segments: First Hawaiian, Inc. operates through three main business segments: Retail Banking, Commercial Banking, and Treasury and Other. Retail Banking serves consumers and small businesses with deposit, lending, and wealth management services. Commercial Banking focuses on middle-market and large businesses, offering commercial loans, real estate lending, and dealer financing. Treasury and Other includes asset/liability management, investment securities, and corporate functions.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FHB relies on a combination of traditional branch banking, digital banking platforms (including online and mobile banking), and a robust core banking system (with a new core system implementation underway). The bank uses advanced risk management, credit scoring, and data analytics for underwriting and portfolio management, and leverages third-party technology providers for payment processing, card services, and cybersecurity.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The bank primarily serves consumers, small businesses, and middle-market to large commercial clients. Key end markets include individuals, real estate developers, auto dealers, and businesses in Hawaii, Guam, and Saipan, with a focus on sectors such as tourism, real estate, retail, and government-related entities.
categories.geographic_coverage: FHB is headquartered in Honolulu, Hawaii, and operates 54 branches across Hawaii (49), Guam (3), and Saipan (2). The majority of its business is concentrated in Hawaii, with additional operations and lending activities in Guam, Saipan, and select U.S. mainland markets (notably in auto dealer financing and commercial real estate).
categories.supply_chain_position: FHB operates as a downstream financial services provider, directly serving end customers (consumers and businesses) with banking, lending, and wealth management products. It does not manufacture physical goods but acts as a financial intermediary and service provider within the financial services supply chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The bank’s strategic focus includes deepening customer relationships through cross-selling, enhancing digital and mobile banking capabilities, and maintaining high service quality. Innovation priorities include technology upgrades (such as a new core banking system), expanding digital offerings, and ongoing investment in cybersecurity and data privacy. FHB also emphasizes risk management, talent development, and diversity and inclusion.
categories.revenue_model: FHB generates revenue primarily through net interest income from loans and investment securities, as well as noninterest income from service charges, card fees, wealth management, trust services, and merchant processing. Additional revenue streams include fees from mortgage origination, loan sales, and investment advisory services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FHB is the largest full-service bank headquartered in Hawaii, competing with local and national commercial banks, savings banks, credit unions, and non-bank financial services firms. Major competitors include Bank of Hawaii, American Savings Bank, and large mainland banks expanding into Hawaii. FHB’s market leadership is based on its asset size, deposit base, and longstanding customer relationships.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2021, FHB had $25.0 billion in assets, $13.0 billion in loans, $21.8 billion in deposits, and $2.7 billion in stockholders’ equity. Net income for 2021 was $265.7 million, up 43% from 2020, reflecting recovery from pandemic impacts. The bank maintains strong capital ratios and a stable, core deposit-funded balance sheet, with growth constrained by its dominant market share in Hawaii.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: FHB emphasizes comprehensive, relationship-based banking with a focus on high-quality customer service, local market expertise, and a broad product suite. Its differentiation lies in its deep roots in Hawaii, strong brand reputation, extensive branch network, and ability to offer both traditional and digital banking solutions tailored to local consumer and business needs.
